judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures are exact. Every problem on this sheet prints model work as a required response and only the final total is checked: problem 1 prints 'Tens altogether: ___' and 'Ones altogether: ___' above the answer blank and verify.json id 1 is a single eval for 38; problem 3 prints the same two subtotal slots plus 'circle them and swap them for one ten' and gets one eval for 65; problem 2 says 'Label each jump you make' and problem 4 says 'Write the number you land on after each jump', neither of which is verified; problems 5 and 7 print the compensation step (+1, +2) on the sheet and check only the compensated total. On the second claim, problem 8 prints two slots - 'What went wrong?' and the corrected total - and verify.json contains no manual entry at all, which is why gate_log.txt ends 'BUILD PASSED - all gates green' with no exit-2 manual banner and final_response.md asserts '8 of 8 machine-verified, 0 manual'. The minor delivery claim is also correct and I can name its origin: final_response.md says '5 pages', gate_log.txt line 92 passes 'page budget: 5' to the compiler and line 94 reports the actual '4 page(s)' - the budget argument was copied into the prose instead of the compiled count.

strengths_to_preserve: The place-value models are drawn, not decorated: problem 1's two block groups sit above 'Tens altogether / Ones altogether' slots that force the decomposition onto paper, problem 3 asks the child to circle ten ones and trade them, and problems 5 and 7 print the compensation amount (+1, +2) beside the number it moves. The judge confirmed the rendered models are unclipped with usable writing space; that is the concept-models mode being taken seriously.

The verify encodings for problems 5 and 7 express the strategy rather than the answer: "(a + b) + (c - b)" at a=39, b=1, c=24 and "(a + c + b) - b" at a=47, c=28, b=2. The check would fail if compensation were not given back, so the method - not just the sum - is inside the gate.

Problem 6's estimate check carries two distinguishable traps (92 from adding the exact numbers, 80 from rounding 58 down), and the study guide's Skill 4 teaches exactly that rounding rule with its own worked example and try-it, so the estimation facet is supported end to end.

root_causes.description: The coverage gate is defined per problem id, not per printed response. verify.py fails only when some id in 1..problem_count has no entry at all, so a problem that prints several required responses is fully satisfied by one scalar check, and both the gate log and the delivery message then describe the sheet as completely verified.
evidence: verify.json holds exactly 8 entries for 8 problems, one scalar per problem, while the worksheet prints between two and four required responses per problem.
worksheet problems 1 and 3 each print 'Tens altogether:' and 'Ones altogether:' slots that no entry covers.
worksheet problem 4 asks the student to 'Write the number you land on after each jump' - a sequence of intermediate values - and only the final 84 is checked.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells the author to reframe error-analysis items 'via the ordinary types' and, a few lines later, to use manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. Nothing states that an item doing both needs both entries, and no gate enforces it, so the explanation slot is dropped and the sheet reports zero manual items.
evidence: worksheet problem 8: 'Explain in one sentence what went wrong, then write the correct total', with a separate 'What went wrong?' slot printed above the answer line; verify.json id 8 is an eval for 73 with a trap and no manual entry.
verify.json contains zero manual entries, so machine_observation records gate_chain_manual_flags: false and the build reports all-green.
problem 2's 'Label each jump you make' is a marked/drawn representation, which SKILL.md itself lists under manual, yet it is neither checked nor flagged.

root_causes.description: final_response.md is composed by hand rather than derived from verify.json and gate_log.txt, so its factual claims about verification coverage, manual items and page counts drift from the artifacts they describe.
evidence: final_response.md: 'Worksheet ... 8 problems, 5 pages' while pdfinfo reports 4 pages; gate_log.txt line 92 shows 5 was the page BUDGET passed to the compiler and line 94 shows the compiled count was 4.
final_response.md: 'Worksheet JSON: 8 of 8 machine-verified, 0 manual' on a sheet whose problem 8 asks for a written explanation.

improvements.title: Make verification coverage per printed response slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: verify.py's coverage gate currently passes as soon as every id in 1..problem_count carries one entry (scripts/verify.py, the `missing = [i for i in range(1, problem_count + 1) if i not in ids]` check). Replace that with a slot-level contract: add a build gate that counts the response slots a problem actually prints (each \ansline/\answerline/\ansblank, each \underline{} write-on rule in a stem, each lettered part (a)/(b)/(c), each row of a fill-in table or partially blank sequence) and fails the build unless that id declares at least as many verify entries. Add the matching rule to SKILL.md's JSON-format paragraph, which today only says 'every problem id 1..N has at least one check'. Here the gate must count the 'Tens altogether' and 'Ones altogether' slots in problems 1 and 3, the per-jump landing numbers in problem 4, and the two slots in problem 8.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/check_answer_slots.py plus a fixture pair under tests/fixtures/: a worksheet .tex whose problem 1 prints two response slots (an inline \underline{} line inside the stem and \problem's automatic answer blank) and a verify.json carrying a single scalar entry for id 1. The gate must exit 1 naming 'problem 1 prints 2 response slots but declares 1 check'. Today build.sh runs that fixture green, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the dominant hard-failure class in this shard: a worksheet can no longer print several required responses per problem while reporting itself fully verified.
improvements.risk: Slot counting is a heuristic over LaTeX and prose, so it will over-count on stems that use \underline for emphasis. Keep it a fail-with-named-slot gate (never a silent skip) and allow an explicit per-problem "slots" override in the verify JSON so a genuine one-slot problem can declare that rather than being blocked.

improvements.title: Require a paired manual entry for every explain / name-the-error / mark-it response
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md carries two rules that pull in opposite directions: the reframing paragraph says error analysis should be encoded 'via the ordinary types - the planted wrong result is checkably wrong and the correction checkably right', while the paragraph eight lines later says to use manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. Authors resolve that by encoding only the numeric correction and dropping the explanation slot. Rewrite the reframing paragraph to state the pairing explicitly: an error-analysis or model-completion item that ALSO prints an explain / name-the-error / circle / cross-out / draw / label slot needs BOTH the typed check for the correction AND a manual entry for that slot under the same id (the curr-088 and curr-100 verify files in this same shard are the worked pattern). Back it with the slot gate so the rule is mechanical, not advisory. Problem 8's 'What went wrong?' and problem 2's 'Label each jump' are the two slots that need manual entries here.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/check_answer_slots.py with a fixture whose problem stem contains an imperative open-response verb ('Explain in one sentence', 'Circle', 'Draw', 'Label', 'Cross out', 'Which measurement did ... actually find?') and whose verify.json entry for that id is a bare eval. The gate must exit 1 demanding a paired {"type": "manual"} entry. The same fixture passes once the manual entry is added. Today it passes in both states, so the test fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The build's manual-item count becomes trustworthy: exit 2 and the 'flagged manual-review items' banner appear whenever a sheet asks a child to explain, mark or draw something, instead of the build reporting all-green on unreviewed reasoning.
improvements.risk: More sheets exit 2 rather than 0, which looks like a regression on dashboards that treat exit 0 as success. That is the intended trust signal; document it in the build-driver section of SKILL.md so exit 2 is not read as a failure.

improvements.title: Take page counts in the delivery message from the compiler, not the budget
improvements.proposed_change: build.sh prints both the page budget it passes to the compiler ('page budget: 5') and the compiled count the engine log reports ('4 page(s), within the 5-page budget'). The delivery step must quote the second. Emit a single machine-readable line per document at the end of the gate log - e.g. 'PAGES ws=4 ak=2 ss=2' - and require the final response to use those numbers.
improvements.regression_test: Add a check to tests/check_prose_consistency.py that fails when a page count asserted in final_response.md disagrees with the compiled count in the same run's gate_log.txt. This case's response ('5 pages' against a compiled 4) fails it; curr-100's response ('worksheet 5 (budget 6)') passes.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a class of delivery statements that are checkably false against the shipped PDF - the cheapest possible credibility loss.
improvements.risk: None; the numbers already exist in the log.

case_summary: This is genuinely strong grade 2-3 place-value addition instruction: every one of the eight problems carries a model tied to notation, the arithmetic is correct throughout (38, 59, 65, 84, 63, about 90, 75, 73), and two of the verify encodings express the compensation strategy rather than just its result. What sinks it is that the model work the sheet exists to elicit - tens and ones subtotals, labelled number-line jumps, the regrouping trade, the friendly-ten adjustment - sits entirely outside the verification record, and problem 8's written explanation is counted among the machine-verified items, producing a build that reports zero manual work on a sheet that demands it. A small, separate defect: the delivery message reports the page budget (5) as if it were the compiled page count (4).
